You are part of an optimization system that improves text (i.e., variable). You will be asked to creatively and critically improve prompts, solutions to problems, code, or any other text-based variable. You will receive some feedback, and use the feedback to improve the variable. The feedback may be noisy, identify what is important and what is correct. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. This is very important: You MUST give your response by sending the improved variable between <IMPROVED_VARIABLE> {improved variable} </IMPROVED_VARIABLE> tags. The text you send between the tags will directly replace the variable.


### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <FEEDBACK>: The feedback to the variable.
# - <CONVERSATION>: The conversation history.
# - <FOCUS>: The focus of the optimization.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.

1. The chosen response provides a more comprehensive list of games that meet the specified criteria. It includes additional games that were not included in the rejected response.
2. The chosen response organizes the information in a clear and structured manner, making it easy for the user to understand.

1. The chosen response does not include the local time for each game, which may be important for users who need that information.
2. The chosen response does not include the season for each game, which may be important for users who need that information.

Strengths of the Rejected Response:
1. The rejected response includes the local time and game score for each game, which may be important for users who need that information.

Weaknesses of the Rejected Response:
1. The rejected response does not provide a comprehensive list of games that meet the specified criteria. It only includes a limited number of games, leaving out other important games.
2. The rejected response does not organize the information in a clear and structured manner, making it difficult for the user to understand. </LM_OUTPUT>

</CONVERSATION>

<FEEDBACK>Since language models have the potential to provide a more comprehensive and organized list of games, adding additional games that meet the specified criteria and organizing the information in a clearer and more structured manner could improve the objective function. For instance, including the local time and game score for each game, as well as organizing the information in a table format, could make the response more user-friendly and comprehensive.</FEEDBACK>

</CONTEXT>
